3 نَاطَحَا , inf. n. نِطَاحٌ (L, Msb) and مُنَاطَحَةٌ, (Msb,) They two (rams or he-goats) smote each other with their horns. (L.) ―
-b2- بَيْنَهُمَا نِطَاحٌ (tropical:) [Between them two is a contention like that of two rams]; said of two learned men, and of two merchants. (A.) ―
-b3- جَرَى لَنَا فِى السُّوقِ نِطَاحٌ (tropical:) [There happened to us in the market a contention like that of two rams]. (A.) ―
-b4- [نَاطَحَهُ He, or it, faced, or was or came opposite to him, or it]: نِطَاحٌ is syn. with مُقَابَلَةٌ in the dial. of El-Hijáz. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
